hints: Since $\angle ABC = 90^\circ$, the perpendicular gradient of $BC$ must be $m_{BC} = -1$.
walkthrough:
Use the right angle to fix the vertex, then locate the perpendicular height.
Calculate gradient $m_{AB}$ and find the perpendicular gradient $m_{BC}$:
$$m_{AB} = \dfrac{6 - 1}{2 - (-3)} = \dfrac{5}{5} = 1$$
$$m_{BC} = -\dfrac{1}{m_{AB}} = -1$$

Set up the gradient of $BC$ with $B(2, 6)$ and $C(k, 1)$:
$$m_{BC} = \dfrac{1 - 6}{k - 2} = \dfrac{-5}{k - 2}$$
$$\dfrac{-5}{k - 2} = -1 \implies k - 2 = 5 \implies k = 7$$

hints: The sides meeting at $B$ are perpendicular, so they can be base and height.
$AC$ is horizontal. Its perpendicular through $B$ is vertical.
walkthrough:
Use the right angle to fix the vertex, then locate the perpendicular height.
With $k=7$, $AB=BC=\sqrt{5^2+5^2}=5\sqrt2$.
The right angle makes these a base-height pair. Area $=\frac12(5\sqrt2)(5\sqrt2)=25$.
Both endpoints of $AC$ have $y=1$. A perpendicular through $B(2,6)$ has $x=2$, so its foot is $M(2,1)$.
